Nigeria DHS 1990-2024: Exploratory Data Analysis

Six survey rounds, 49 recode files, weighted design-based estimates

24 October 2026

1. What is in the data

This report is generated only after the supplied DHS ZIP archives have been verified and materialised to data/unpacked/<survey year>/. The six archives contain 49 SPSS files with 2,202,226 records in total (81,035 variable columns across files). Each round has the standard DHS recodes; newer rounds add files (couples, pregnancies, fieldworkers, postnatal).

The inventory is evidence of the extracted files used for this report, rather than a claim that R reads SPSS files directly from the ZIP archives.

Data quality checks

  • Weights: every analytic file carries a DHS weight (v005, hv005, mv005); mean normalised weights are ~1.00 as expected.
  • Clusters: 298 (1990), 362 (2003), 886 (2008), 896 (2013), 1,389 (2018) and ~1,380 (2024) - sample design grew strongly over time.
  • Missingness is high (40-90% of cells) but almost entirely structural: questions apply only to sub-groups (e.g. married women, recent births) and the files keep empty slots for repeated sections (up to 20 births per woman). It should not be read as poor data quality.
  • Survey content changes: number of variables per file roughly doubled since 1990, so not every indicator is comparable across all rounds.

The full per-variable dictionary (label, % missing, distinct values for every variable in every file) is in tables/01_variable_dictionary_all_files.csv.

3. Women 15-49

Key observations

  • Women are steadily more urban (25% in 1990 to 48% in 2024) and more educated (secondary+ rose from 19% to 55%), although around a third still have no schooling - a share that has barely moved since 2008.
  • Completed fertility (children ever born at 40-49) has fallen from ~6.5-6.8 to 5.5, and the age at first birth has risen to 20.4.
  • Modern contraceptive use among married women rose from 3.5% to 15.3%, but remains low and strongly patterned by wealth and zone.

Harmonising the six geopolitical zones

  • 2003-2024 already code region as the six zones; only the label capitalisation differs (e.g. 2024 “South west”), which is normalised.
  • 1990 codes only four regions, but records the 1990 state of residence (21 states + Abuja). Each 1990 state lies wholly inside one present-day zone (later splits such as Bendel to Edo/Delta or Gongola to Adamawa/Taraba stay in the same zone), so women were assigned to zones from their state. Every 1990 woman was assigned.
Unweighted number of women per zone

North East 747 1,413 6,217 6,630 7,639 6,338
North West 2,266 1,791 7,297 9,673 10,129 9,404

In 1990 modern contraception ranged from under 1% in the North East and North West to 10% in the South West; by 2024 the South West reached 31% while the North West is still about 9%.

Spatial-boundary scope

This EDA uses DHS region variables to tabulate zone estimates; it does not use a shapefile to calculate those estimates. The supplied shape archives are reserved for post-estimation mapping in the SAP pipeline. Only the survey-matched six-zone boundaries for 2003–2024 are appropriate for those maps. The 1990 archive contains four non-comparable regions and must not be displayed as a six-zone map; the 1999 and 2025 archives are outside this analysis scope. The 2024 geometry has invalid polygons that must be repaired with sf::st_make_valid() before display, without altering the associated DHS estimates.

4. Men

Men are consistently more educated than women (only ~22% with no education vs ~35% for women). The 2013 male sample is 15-49 whereas other rounds include older men, which explains the dip in mean age that year.

5. Children under 5

  • Stunting fell from 49% (1990) to 42% (2003) and 37% (2013/2018), then rose again to 39% in 2024; it is 3-4 times higher in the poorest (~55%) than the richest quintile (~15%).
  • Wasting dropped from 14-18% (2008/2013) to 7-8%.
  • The crude share of recent births who died before age 5 fell from ~13-14% (1990/2003) to ~8.5% (2024).

Linking 1990 and 2003 height/weight files

For 1990 and 2003 the WHO z-scores sit in separate HW files. They were linked to the children’s file following DHS MERGE.DOC: 1990 (measured children of interviewed women) on HWCASEID + HWLINE = CASEID + MIDX; 2003 (measured at household level) on HWHHID + HWLINE = HHID + B16, where HHID is the first 12 characters of CASEID. No child was duplicated.

Year File Link key HW records Children (KR) Children linked Valid height-for-age KR children not linked
1990 NGHW21FL.SAV HWCASEID+HWLINE = CASEID+MIDX 7902 7902 7902 5496 0
2003 NGHW4BFL.SAV HWHHID+HWLINE = HHID+B16 5677 6029 4981 4282 1048

The linkage count is determined from the merge keys, and valid HAZ is reported separately. A linked record may legitimately have no usable measurement (for example, a special code); missing or flagged HAZ must not be labelled as an unmatched child. The KR-based estimates necessarily exclude children absent from the KR file and records with invalid anthropometry.

Linking the 1990 wealth index (WI file)

The 1990 survey ships its wealth index as a separate WI file (household ID, factor score, quintile). It was linked on WHHID = HHID, where HHID is the first 12 characters of CASEID, so all wealth breakdowns now start in 1990.

Year Linked to WI file Link key Records Matched
1990 IR NGWI21FL.SAV WHHID = HHID (CASEID chars 1-12) 8781 8781
1990 KR NGWI21FL.SAV WHHID = HHID (CASEID chars 1-12) 7902 7902

In 1990 stunting differed little by wealth (about 52-54% in the bottom three quintiles, 37% in the richest); by 2024 the gap had widened to about 56% vs 15%. Modern contraception in 1990 was under 2% outside the richest quintile (12%).

6. Limitations

  • 1990 and 2003 anthropometry covers measured children of the children’s file only; official DHS reports may use household-based samples, so small differences are expected.
  • The births-based mortality figure is a crude proportion, not the official DHS life-table under-5 mortality rate.
  • 1990 has no men’s file. Its wealth index comes from the separate WI file and uses DHS’s original 1990 construction, so quintiles are relative within each survey.
  • 1990 zones are rebuilt from state of residence; the 1990 sample was not designed for zone-level estimates, so its zone confidence intervals are wider.
  • Zone tables are based on DHS region variables. They are not spatial analyses and should not be interpreted as evidence of geographic clustering. Shapefiles are used only for survey-matched, post-estimation SAP maps.
  • This EDA is descriptive. It does not estimate causal effects or substitute for DHS’s official indicator definitions and reporting procedures.
